structured_output.summary: All-sector fit landed on wrong period (1.4372686 vs 1.430446 d); refit and S113–114 decide.
reasons: The step 9 fit did not fit the detected signal: fit_period_days 1.4372686 differs from period_days 1.430446 and joint_search_period_days 1.430009 by 0.0068 d, which over the S12–S102 baseline is many cycles; its fit_duration_hours 7.784 is eight times the search duration_hours 0.96, its fit_depth_ppm 1102 is a quarter of depth_ppm 3923.1, and fit_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.59 with stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 0.127 is unphysical for a 1.43-day orbit. The all-sector figure shows ramps and partial dips at scattered phases, not a transit.

Because the step 9 ephemeris is wrong, its derived values are unreliable: planet_radius_earth_radii 6.65, fit_impact_parameter 0.029, odd_even_difference_sigma 0.81, secondary_depth_ppm 75 +/- 28, depth_ppm_by_sector (sector_depth_consistency_p_value 5.42e-12), and the cutout depths that are negative in S12, S65 and S66 (cutout_sector_depth_consistency_p_value 4.32e-105). The cautions 'depths differ between sectors' and 'dip longer than a transit at this period' are artefacts of this fit, so I disagree with the mechanical decision's basis, though not with its outcome of held.

The signal itself is real and on the target: MES 34.77244 with 15 transits in S101; joint_search_detected True with joint_search_snr 84.7 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 13.7; other_sector_results show SNR close to expected in all eight other sectors; pixel_verdict on target in S99, S100, S101 and S102 (SNR 8.3, 19.5, 15.7, 23.6) and joint_pixel_verdict on target with joint_difference_image_snr 35.4 and joint_best_source TIC 425809198. The S99–S102 difference images show the dip on the target pixel.

The nature of the signal is undecided: transit_grazing True with companion_radius_earth_radii 14.93697 (the grazing geometry leaves the radius almost unconstrained), a 0.96-hour dip of 3923.1 ppm at 1.43 d on a 1.84658 solar-radius star is as consistent with a grazing stellar companion as with a planet, and TRICERATOPS gives fpp_mean 0.4635 with fpp_standard_deviation 0.45, with most_likely_scenario 'BEBx2P on TIC 425809198'. nfpp_mean 1.646e-13 and nearby_scenarios_excluded True do argue against the neighbours listed in gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip, consistent with the on-target pixel result.

Supporting but not decisive: gaia_ruwe 0.78, gaia_non_single_star 0, gaia_eclipsing_binary False, no vsx_variables or vsx_binaries, period_pile_up_ratio 0.9, ephemeris_match_likely_sources empty, and no exofop_tois, exofop_ctois or published_signal, so the candidate is new.

What would decide it: re-run the all-sector fit fixed near period_days 1.430446 and duration_hours 0.96 to obtain a valid odd-even test, secondary-eclipse test at the correct phase 0.5, and per-sector depth consistency; and unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 113 114 will add 200-s data for the secondary-eclipse and depth tests. A valid fit with no secondary and consistent depths would support submission as a grazing CTOI; a detected secondary or odd-even difference would drop it.
